A total of 549 children with ADHD and 963 healthy controls were enrolled. Skin element levels were measured using a non-invasive high-throughput technique. Behavioral assessments were performed using the CONNERS, SNAP‑IV, SCARED, and WEISS scales. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with age as a covariate was used to compare intergroup differences in element levels. Partial correlation analysis was applied to control for age as a confounding factor. The Benjamini‑Hochberg method was used to control the false discovery rate (FDR) for multiple comparison correction, with a significance threshold of q < 0.05. After adjusting for age and FDR correction, 28 elements showed significant differences between the ADHD group and the control group. In the ADHD group, essential/potentially beneficial elements such as Mg, Zn, I, Cr, Li and Ge were decreased, whereas B and harmful elements including Pb, Hg, Cd, As, Al, Be, and Ba were increased. Multiple elements exhibited stable associations with inattention, hyperactivity-impulsivity, anxiety, and risk-taking behavior. Children with ADHD displayed a complex network pattern of synergistic and antagonistic inter-element relationships. Children with ADHD exhibit a characteristic skin trace elementomic imbalance, characterized by decreased beneficial elements and increased harmful elements, which is closely associated with behavioral symptoms. Non-invasive skin elementomics may serve as a reference indicator for population-based risk screening of childhood ADHD and holds promise for population-based screening.

title: miR-21a-5p targets DDX58 to suppress TLR2/NF-κB signaling and protect the blood-brain barrier after injury.
abstract: Damage to the blood-brain barrier (BBB) plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of various neurological disorders. miR-21a-5p has been implicated in the modulation of BBB injury. Understanding the molecular targets of miR-21a-5p is crucial for developing targeted interventions in BBB repair. The target gene of miR-21a-5p was identified through bioinformatics analysis and validated using a dual luciferase reporter assay. The expression of target gene was further confirmed in both in vivo and in vitro models of BBB injury. BBB injury cell models were employed to assess the effects of target gene overexpression and silencing on brain microvascular endothelial cell (BMEC) activity, as well as on the TLR2/NF-κB signaling pathway and associated BBB proteins. miR-21a-5p overexpression and silencing were utilized to assess the impact of target gene on BBB integrity. DDX58 was identified as a direct target of miR-21a-5p and is shown to modulate BBB injury. DDX58 expression was found to be upregulated in models of BBB damage. Exosomes containing miR-21a-5p mitigated BBB damage, which was associated with downregulated DDX58 expression in vivo and in vitro. Overexpression of DDX58 in BMECs resulted in reduced cellular viability, increased expression of TLR2 and phosphorylated p65 (p-p65), as well as elevated levels of matrix metalloproteinases (MMP-2/9), which are associated with BBB disruption. This was accompanied by a reduction in tight junction proteins, including claudin-5, occludin, and ZO-1. Conversely, silencing DDX58 expression exhibited the opposite effects. Both miR-21a-5p treatment and DDX58 interference alleviated BBB injury. Co-overexpression of DDX58 during miR-21a-5p treatment reversed the protective effects of miR-21a-5p, exacerbating BBB injury. miR-21a-5p targets and downregulates DDX58, which is associated with reduced expression of TLR2/NF-κB-related markers, decreased MMP-2/9 levels, and protection of tight junction integrity.

title: Molecular Mechanisms of Immunomodulation by Neural Stem Cells in Spinal Cord Injury: From Macrophage Polarization to Therapeutic Plasticity.
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers a chronic neuroinflammatory cascade driven by persistent M1 macrophage polarization, creating a hostile microenvironment that inhibits axonal regeneration and perpetuates secondary tissue damage. Neural stem cells (NSCs) offer a promising therapeutic strategy through immunomodulation, reshaping the inflammatory landscape rather than merely replacing lost neurons. This review synthesizes evidence on the molecular mechanisms by which NSCs reprogram the immune response. NSCs suppress TLR4/NF-κB signaling to shift macrophages from a neurotoxic M1 phenotype toward a pro-regenerative M2 phenotype, engage in reciprocal dialogue with T cells and microglia to create a neurogenic niche, secrete neurotrophic factors that upregulate KCC2 and restore GABAergic inhibition, and modulate purinergic signaling to attenuate neuropathic pain. However, the evidence base remains incomplete. Most studies provide correlative rather than causal evidence, and the M1/M2 framework does not fully capture macrophage heterogeneity after SCI, particularly in the chronic phase where foam cells, pro-fibrotic phenotypes, and disease-associated subpopulations emerge. The subacute window is generally associated with superior outcomes, but optimal timing varies with injury severity, model, cell source, transplantation route, and cell dose. Clinical translation remains at an early stage; phase I trials have established feasibility and short-term safety, but most lacked control groups and adequate sample sizes. Adverse effects, including allodynia, tumorigenicity, and immune-related complications, underscore that neural cell transplantation is not inherently safe. Future progress requires adequately powered trials with objective endpoints, biomarker development, refined immunomodulation strategies, and careful monitoring for adverse effects.

title: Transcranial Evoked Potentials are Minimally Influenced by Afferent Feedback From Peripheral Muscle Contraction.
abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation with electroencephalography (TMS-EEG) investigates cortical reactivity, yet the contribution of sensory feedback from muscle twitches to the recorded signals remains debated. We combined M1 TMS-EEG with electromyography, accelerometry, and peripheral electrical stimulation to dissociate central and peripheral contributions. We compared EEG responses across trials yielding large versus small motor outputs, while peripheral stimulation isolated pure afferent components. Bayesian analysis revealed that larger motor outputs covaried with distinct EEG morphologies uniformly across all time windows-including those too early for peripheral feedback-indicating that spontaneous fluctuations in baseline motor cortex excitability drive both responses. Conversely, isolated muscle contraction produced delayed (> 65 ms), markedly smaller EEG responses with distinct spatiotemporal profiles. We conclude that sensory feedback from muscle twitches contributes minimally to TMS-evoked EEG responses, which instead primarily reflect the baseline excitability state of the stimulated cortex.

title: Correction: Comparative MRI analysis of the forebrain of three sauropsida models.
Heart rate variability and cortisol responses to acute low- and moderate-intensity exercise in stress-related exhaustion.
abstract: Exercise is commonly recommended to support stress regulation and mental health, yet it remains unclear whether these benefits translate to conditions characterized by prolonged stress and fatigue. The aims were to examine whether autonomic and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis responses to a single exercise bout differ between individuals with stress-related exhaustion and healthy controls, and whether responses vary by exercise intensity. In a randomized, counterbalanced crossover design, 30 individuals with stress-related exhaustion (93.3% women; age 46.3 ± 5.89) and 29 healthy controls with a comparable age and sex distribution (93.1% women; age 45.5 ± 5.47) completed two 22-min cycling sessions at workloads corresponding to 40% (low intensity) and 55% (moderate intensity) of estimated maximal oxygen uptake (V̇O₂max) on separate occasions. Heart rate variability (HRV; RMSSD, SD2/SD1, LF/HF) and salivary cortisol were assessed pre-exercise, post-exercise, and 30 min post-exercise, with HRV also assessed during exercise. Compared with controls, individuals with stress-related exhaustion showed lower RMSSD overall, with the most apparent between-group differences observed during the post-exercise period. Within the exhaustion group, moderate- compared with low-intensity exercise was associated with lower RMSSD and higher SD2/SD1 and LF/HF, whereas no intensity effects were observed in controls. No between-group differences were observed in HRV during exercise. Cortisol analyses suggested overall group-related differences, without clear differences across time points. These findings suggest altered physiological stress-system regulation in stress-related exhaustion and highlight the post-exercise period and exercise intensity as important considerations when tailoring exercise recommendations for this population. The study was retrospectively registered on 05/30/2024 at Clinical Trials.gov, with trial registration number NCT06429423.

title: [On the way to tobacco- and nicotine-free healthcare institutions].
abstract: Tobacco use and recreational nicotine consumption remain among the leading preventable causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, including in Hungary. The World Health Organization Framework Convention on Tobacco Control and related international recommendations identify healthcare institutions as key actors in tobacco control. To support the implementation of comprehensive tobacco- and nicotine-free healthcare services, the Global Network for Tobacco Free Healthcare Services (GNTH) has developed an evidence-based framework consisting of 8 standards and a structured institutional self-audit tool. However, no Hungarian-language version of this methodology has previously been available. This study aims to present the Hungarian linguistic and cultural adaptation process of the English version of the self-audit tool developed by the GNTH and the Spanish implementation guide. Linguistic and cultural adaptation of the English-language GNTH self-audit tool and the Spanish implementation guide were conducted. The adaptation process considered the Hungarian legal, policy and healthcare system context. Content validation was supported by expert review, while practical applicability was assessed through pilot testing in a tertiary healthcare institution. The adaptation followed an iterative process involving consultations with representatives of the GNTH Board. The adaptation process resulted in the development of the complete Hungarian GNTH audit package, including the institutional self-audit questionnaire, scoring template, and a detailed implementation guide tailored to the characteristics of the Hungarian healthcare system. The final tool enables objective assessment of tobacco- and nicotine-free institutional performance based on 8 GNTH standards, 48 assessment criteria, and 192 scoring specifications. The Hungarian adaptation was formally reviewed and acknowledged by the GNTH Executive Board. The Hungarian GNTH self-audit tool represents a novel quality improvement and management instrument for healthcare organizations. Its implementation may facilitate the transition from passive regulatory compliance towards a proactive, systems-based and data-driven institutional approach to tobacco and nicotine control. The methodology also provides a foundation for benchmarking, continuous quality improvement, and the future development of a national professional network supporting tobacco-free healthcare services. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(43): 1739-1748.

title: O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine homeostasis in brain health and disease: From physiology to neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders.
abstract: Protein O-GlcNAcylation is a dynamic and reversible post-translational modification that functions as a central nutrient-sensing mechanism linking cellular metabolism to protein function. Controlled by the opposing activities of O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine transferase and O-GlcNAcase, O-GlcNAcylation regulates thousands of nuclear, cytoplasmic, synaptic, and mitochondrial proteins involved in gene expression, neuronal differentiation, synaptic plasticity, proteostasis, mitochondrial homeostasis, and neuroimmune signaling. The brain exhibits particularly high O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine activity, reflecting its exceptional metabolic demands and the need to rapidly couple nutrient availability with neuronal function. Emerging evidence demonstrates that precise regulation of O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine cycling is indispensable throughout the lifespan, from embryonic neurodevelopment to healthy brain aging. Conversely, disruption of O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine homeostasis caused by genetic defects, metabolic disturbances, or environmental stress contributes to neurodevelopmental disorders. In the aging brain, impaired glucose metabolism and insulin resistance reduce O-GlcNAcylation, promoting mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, proteostasis failure, and the accumulation of pathogenic proteins. Consequently, dysregulated O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine signaling has emerged as a convergent mechanism underlying brain disorders spanning neurodevelopment to neurodegeneration. Although clinical translation remains challenging, growing evidence supports O-GlcNAcylation as a master regulator of brain homeostasis and a promising therapeutic target for neurological disorders. Collectively, this review highlights O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine signaling as a molecular bridge connecting early brain development, adulthood, and aging, providing an integrated framework for understanding brain physiology and disease.

title: Membrane targeted rabies virus labeling system: Brain-wide single-neuron mapping of target-specific and intersectionally defined neuronal circuits.
abstract: Elucidating neural circuit organization at single-neuron resolution is a core goal of modern neuroscience. Brain-wide input connectivity maps underpin the mammalian connectome, but systematic and comprehensive whole-brain input mapping with resolved single-neuron anatomy for defined brain regions remains a formidable technical challenge. Here, we developed a membrane-targeted rabies virus labeling system using mClover3 as the fluorescent reporter, which features high compatibility with fluorescence micro-optical sectioning tomography imaging and enables complete visualization of fine neuronal morphology across the entire brain. Validation in the mouse primary somatosensory cortex barrel field confirms robust full-morphology labeling and faithful reconstruction of brain-wide input neurons, revealing diverse projection patterns with distinct axonal targets. We further generated a dual-recombinase dependent TVA reporter mouse line to enable anatomical interrogation of intersectionally defined neuron populations via EnvA-pseudotyped membrane-targeted rabies virus, allowing specific targeting and single-neuron reconstruction of PV+/vGlut2+ L5b pyramidal neurons in the primary somatosensory cortex barrel field. These neurons exhibited a pathway-conserved population-level projection profile likely representing a subset of pyramidal tract neuron projections, while showing pronounced cellto-cell diversity in axonal target specificity. Overall, this work delivers a robust, versatile toolkit for brain-wide single-neuron mapping of target-specific and intersectionally defined neuronal circuits, with strong potential to advance brain connectomics.

title: Ventilation inhomogeneity in Duchenne muscular dystrophy before the initiation of ventilatory support: Insights from electrical impedance tomography.
abstract: Prior to the onset of overt ventilatory failure, patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) can display non-uniform respiratory mechanics, resulting from atelectasis in small lung regions secondary to rapid, shallow breathing and/or peripheral airway obstruction, thereby predisposing to the development of ventilation inhomogeneity. To investigate ventilation distribution in DMD patients before the initiation of long-term assisted ventilation by using electrical impedance tomography (EIT). Patients and interventions: Eighteen DMD patients underwent EIT between 1 January and 31 December 2025. Primary study endpoint: Global Inhomogeneity Index (GI). EIT data were compared with those obtained from a group of 11 healthy, similarly aged male medical residents. GI was significantly higher in the DMD patients with respect to healthy males [0.44 ± 0.13 (0.36-0.77) vs 0.37 ± 0.03 (0.32-0.43); p < 0.001]. A GI of 0.5 maximised the distinction between DMD patients with a ventilation distribution pattern similar to or different from the healthy subjects. Before initiation of assisted ventilation, a subset of DMD patients may develop lung ventilation inhomogeneity, which can be readily assessed by means of EIT. Whether such inhomogeneity is predictive of major clinical events therefore constitutes a critical question to be addressed.

title: Two clinical trajectories in general adult psychiatry: divergent service use and mortality.
abstract: Psychiatric in-patient populations are heterogeneous. Severe and enduring psychiatric illness (SEPI) and trauma, stressor-related and substance use (TSRS) presentations differ clinically, but their service demands and mortality within one system are poorly characterised. To characterise in-patient service use and mortality across clinical trajectories in one National Health Service general adult psychiatry (GAP) service. Longitudinal cohort study of 5204 in-patient episodes (2016-2024) aggregated to 2665 patients classified as SEPI (schizophrenia spectrum, bipolar disorder, severe unipolar depression) or TSRS, the latter subdivided into borderline personality disorder (BPD) and non-psychotic mood, stress-related and substance-use presentations. Analyses used person-years, standardised mortality ratios (SMRs), survival analysis and years of life lost. SEPI comprised 28.9% of patients but 69.3% of bed utilisation, with longer, recurrent admissions. TSRS presentations were brief and crisis-driven; BPD had the highest admission frequency with short stays. Cumulative mortality was 53% higher in SEPI than TSRS (13.5 v. 8.8%), but after adjustment for age and illness duration mortality was similar across groups (SMR 4.87). TSRS deaths occurred at younger ages, particularly in BPD, whereas SEPI deaths reflected common physical illnesses occurring far earlier than in the general population. Most deaths (98.5%) occurred outside in-patient settings. GAP services accommodate two trajectories with contrasting demands but similarly high mortality (SMR 4.87): enduring, medically managed illness with high cumulative resource use, and episodic brief crisis presentations. Recognising this is essential for service design, since current models combine structurally distinct demands within a single system.

title: Associations between cognition and functioning: examining the role of mental health in clinically ascertained and population-based samples.
abstract: Cognitive function is a significant predictor of daily functioning in the population, yet the extent to which common mental health symptoms account for this relationship remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the relationship between cognition, mental health and functioning across two cohorts. Participants were recruited from an online population cohort, HealthWise Wales (N = 3679), and a psychiatric cohort, the National Centre for Mental Health (NCMH, N = 1036), to complete a cognitive battery and the World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS). We assessed the associations between cognitive performance and the WHODAS, as well as two measures of life functioning: current employment and cohabitation with a partner. We examined the role of current mood, psychiatric and neurodevelopmental history and lifestyle factors using linear and logistic regression. Higher cognitive performance was associated with fewer functional difficulties on the WHODAS (HealthWise Wales: B = -0.12, 95% CI (-0.15,-0.09), P < 0.001; NCMH: B = -0.1, 95% CI (-0.13,-0.08), P < 0.001), being in employment or education (HealthWise Wales: odds ratio 1.22, 95% CI (1.11,1.34), P < 0.001; NCMH: odds ratio 1.31, 95% CI (1.19,1.46), P < 0.001) and living with a partner (HealthWise Wales only: odds ratio 1.19, 95% CI (1.06,1.32), P = 0.003). Higher levels of depression and anxiety symptoms were consistently associated with reduced functioning across all analyses. The relationship between cognition and functioning remained significant but attenuated after accounting for these symptoms. Cognitive function was associated with functioning in both clinical and population-derived samples. Current symptoms of depression and anxiety play a key role in this relationship. Both cognitive function and common mental health problems may be potential intervention targets to alleviate daily difficulties.

title: Healthcare use by people with dementia from diagnosis to the end of life: latent class and longitudinal analysis of linked healthcare data.
abstract: The first year after diagnosis and the last year of life are critical periods for people with dementia. To (a) identify subgroups within a large sample of people with dementia, characterised by healthcare use in the year after diagnosis and the last year of life; (b) describe the biopsychosocial characteristics associated with these subgroups; and (c) explore moves between subgroups over time. A retrospective cohort of people diagnosed with dementia in London, UK, was assembled using linked clinical and administrative data-sets. We used latent class analysis to identify subgroups based on hospital and specialist mental healthcare service use in the year following diagnosis and the year before death. We used multinomial logistic regression to describe biopsychosocial characteristics and class membership, and latent transition analysis to explore moves between subgroups. Among 8623 people with dementia, we identified 3 subgroups of healthcare use in the year after diagnosis: 'low use' (49%), 'hospital use' (34%) and 'mental healthcare use' (17%). In the last year of life, four subgroups were identified: 'low use' (32%), 'moderate hospital use' (43%), 'high hospital use' (9%) and 'community healthcare use' (17%). Biopsychosocial factors, including age, ethnicity, and cognitive and physical problems, associated with subgroups differed for the time periods. Male gender, mixed dementia and vascular dementia diagnoses were associated with a higher risk of unplanned hospital use. Transition probabilities indicated unstable patterns of healthcare use after diagnosis and before death. Distinct subgroups and healthcare patterns in two care periods can facilitate proactive, needs-based service provision while potentially reducing emergency hospital use.

title: Patient and caregiver characteristics and outcomes following compulsory admission for anorexia nervosa treatment.
abstract: A proportion of patients with anorexia nervosa require compulsory admission due to treatment refusal in the context of high medical or psychiatric risk. The clinical characteristics and treatment outcomes of patients with anorexia nervosa compulsorily admitted for in-patient care (current and previous) were compared with those of patients admitted voluntarily. The characteristics of their caregivers were also evaluated. This is a secondary analysis of the Transition Care in Anorexia Nervosa Through Guidance Online from Peer and Carer Expertise trial. We included 274 patient-caregiver dyads: 62 on compulsory admission ('current compulsory'), 48 on voluntary admission with a history of compulsory treatment ('previous compulsory') and 164 on voluntary admission without a history of compulsory treatment ('voluntary'). Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics, and longitudinal clinical outcomes at 3-6 and 9-12 months, were compared across groups. Patients in the current compulsory group had an earlier age of onset, a higher proportion of obsessive-compulsive disorder comorbidity and less motivation and confidence to change compared with the voluntary group. The previous compulsory group showed a longer illness duration, older age and lower body mass index (BMI) compared with the other groups. All groups showed improvement, with similar outcomes at the end of the study except for depression symptoms and BMI. Caregivers had varying levels of distress and caregiving skills at baseline, which had improved by the end of the study. People receiving current or previous compulsory treatment presented with diverse clinical presentations. Further studies are needed to determine whether more individualised approaches improve outcomes in these subgroups. Trial registration number and data-set information: ISRCTN14644379.

title: Combining Cognitive Training and Brain Stimulation: A Novel Approach to Address Disordered Eating and Antipsychotic-Induced Weight Gain in People With Severe Mental Illness.
abstract: Antipsychotic-induced weight gain is a distressing side effect that most often occurs within the first 3-6 months of pharmacological initiation, significantly increasing cardiometabolic risk and mortality in individuals with severe mental illness. To assess the feasibility of reducing food craving and binge eating using Approach Bias Modification Training (ABMT) combined with real or sham Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS). In this double-blind, parallel-group, two-arm, sham-controlled trial, adults with schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder on stable doses of antipsychotics were randomly allocated to a total of five ABMT sessions together with either real or sham tDCS administered over 3 weeks. Assessments were made at baseline (T0), post-treatment (T1) and at a 2-week follow-up (T2). Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, attendance, retention, tDCS safety, acceptability, tolerability, and blinding. Secondary outcomes were changes in food craving, binge eating, approach bias to food, body mass index, and psychological symptoms. Twenty-eight participants were recruited (93% of target). Retention was high (T1 = 85.7% and T2 = 78.6%); blinding accuracy was 46.4%. Medium effect sizes favoured 'ABMT + real tDCS' for reducing binge eating (d = -0.6, 95% CI -1.5, 0.3), and 'ABMT + sham tDCS' for reducing food cravings (d = 0.5, 95% CI -0.4, 1.4). Within-groups, only the 'ABMT + real tDCS' arm showed reduced approach bias to food and approach-avoidance bias to food, and increased avoidance bias to food (all p < 0.05). This was followed by reduced binge eating episodes (p < 0.05). Both groups reported frequent binge-eating episodes ('ABMT + tDCS' = 43%; 'ABMT + sham tDCS' = 28.6%). The initiation of antipsychotic therapy is a critical clinical window for early intervention to mitigate the long-term metabolic and psychiatric consequences of antipsychotic-induced weight gain. Combining ABMT + tDCS is acceptable and may help reduce binge eating in individuals on antipsychotics, with a potential synergistic effect between cognitive training and brain stimulation. A confirmatory trial is needed to assess its effectiveness and should include BED diagnosis as a stratification criterion. ISRCTN Identifier: 13280178.

title: A Glycan Key Unlocks Microglia Targeting and Reprogramming to Promote Functional Recovery After Spinal Cord Injury.
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers uncontrolled neuroinflammation driven by dysfunctional microglia and pro-inflammatory-biased reprogramming, yet precise therapeutic strategies remain limited. Here, we report a novel glycan-targeted nanoparticle system (ICT@APD) designed to enhance the microglia-reprogramming potential of icaritin (ICT) while overcoming its inherent narrow therapeutic window. By functionalizing nanoparticles with 2,5-anhydro-D-mannitol (2,5-AM), a high-affinity ligand for the microglia-specific transporter GLUT5, ICT@APD achieves selective microglial uptake and amplifies the capacity of ICT to reprogram microglia toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. The targeted reprogramming consequently creates a positive microenvironment that promotes axon regeneration, neuronal survival, and synaptic reconstruction, leading to significantly improved locomotor recovery after SCI. Our findings establish a novel glycan-mediated microglial targeting and reprogramming strategy for SCI repair, which may extend to other central nervous system disorders and provide a referenceable platform for the delivery of other therapeutic agents with a narrow therapeutic window.

title: Multimodal premotor stimulation during action observation transiently boosts corticospinal excitability and motor performance.
Do psychiatrists have a spider-sense? Clinical impressions as violations of interpersonal Bayesian expectation.
abstract: Psychiatric diagnosis depends on the clinician's ability to infer mental states from complex and dynamically evolving interpersonal signals. During the psychiatric interview, clinicians do not only collect explicit symptoms; they continuously sample a rich array of non-verbal and paralinguistic cues including gaze, prosody, affective reciprocity, and interactional timing. These signals are central to psychiatric assessment, yet their contribution to diagnostic reasoning remains poorly formalized. In this Review, we propose a computational account of clinical impressions in psychiatry. We integrate evidence from phenomenological psychopathology, social cognition, and computational neuroscience. We argue that such impressions may arise when the clinician's generative model of social interaction is persistently disconfirmed by subtle deviations in interpersonal behaviour, generating high-level social prediction errors experienced as a sense of incongruity or failed attunement. We formalize this process as VIBE: Violation of Interpersonal Bayesian Expectation. VIBE denotes a pre-reflective epistemic signal generated when observed interpersonal cues deviate from the clinician's expected model of social reciprocity. It is not a diagnostic criterion but orients hypothesis generation by drawing attention to disturbances in interpersonal predictability. We hypothesize that VIBE may constitute a transdiagnostic mechanism: different disorders, from schizophrenia to autism spectrum disorder and mood disorders, may disrupt distinct dimensions of interpersonal prediction. The Praecox Feeling, first described by Rümke in 1942, can be read as the earliest clinical formalization of this process and as its schizophrenia-spectrum instance, in which the profile of interpersonal violations is consistent enough to be clinically recognizable. This framework recasts the diagnostic impression as an embodied inferential process rather than an opaque subjective faculty. Teaching clinicians to articulate, examine, and recalibrate these impressions could strengthen diagnostic reasoning, reduce bias, and improve therapeutic attunement. VIBE provides a bridge between phenomenological psychopathology and computational neuroscience, and offers a tractable, empirically testable model for studying the neurocomputational basis of psychiatric clinical judgement.

title: Enrichment of In Utero Rhythmic Experience Promotes Postnatal Visuospatial Attention.
journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
abstract: By 2 months of age, infants leverage predictable temporal structures to optimize attention allocation, disengaging faster from rhythmic than nonrhythmic stimuli-a pattern absent in newborns and attributed to postnatal experience. Here, we investigated whether prenatal rhythmic enrichment provides an earlier foundation for this competence. From week 29 until delivery, pregnant women (N = 101) provided fetuses either multisensory rhythmic stimulation (experimental, N = 49) or nonrhythmic relaxation (control, N = 52). Visual attention disengagement was assessed using an overlap task with rhythmic, nonrhythmic, and static stimuli, at birth (N = 30 per group) and 2 months (N = 30 per group). At 2 months, both groups showed the expected attentional cost for nonrhythmic stimuli. At birth, this pattern appeared only in the experimental group, indicating that prenatal rhythmic enrichment accelerates the typical developmental timeline for temporal attention tuning. Individual differences further showed that greater amounts of prenatal rhythmic stimulation predicted faster overall disengagement at birth, and a stronger cost for nonrhythmic stimuli at 2 months. While acknowledging methodological constraints inherent to the population under study, these findings suggest that the developing brain begins to tune to environmental temporal structure prenatally, and that this process is promoted by in utero rhythmic experience.

title: Evaluation of Plasma Spermine and Spermidine Levels in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma and Exfoliation Glaucoma.
abstract: This study aimed to compare plasma spermine and spermidine concentrations in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), patients with exfoliation glaucoma (EG), and healthy individuals, and to explore their potential association with disease severity. This prospective case-control study was conducted at a tertiary referral center and included patients with an established diagnosis of POAG or EG for more than two years. The control group consisted of age- and sex-matched healthy individuals. Participants with predefined systemic comorbidities or ocular conditions that could potentially confound the study findings were excluded. Plasma concentrations of spermine and spermidine were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Glaucoma severity was assessed using the modified Hodapp-Parrish-Anderson glaucoma staging system. Significant differences in spermine and spermidine concentrations were observed among the three study groups (p=0.005 and p=0.037, respectively). Post-hoc analyses showed that spermine levels were significantly elevated in both the POAG and EG groups relative to controls, whereas spermidine levels were significantly increased only in the POAG group. In the EG group, spermidine levels showed a weak inverse correlation with glaucoma severity (Kendall's tau-b=-0.317, p=0.037). The observed alterations in plasma spermine and spermidine concentrations suggest a potential association between systemic polyamine metabolism and glaucoma. Given the proposed roles of polyamines in neurodegenerative processes, further studies are warranted to clarify the biological significance of these findings in glaucoma.

title: CCR1 Antagonism by BX471 Attenuates Neuroinflammation and Apoptosis: Preliminary Findings From an In Vitro Model of Neuronal Injury.
abstract: Neuronal injury as traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers a complex pathophysiological cascade involving inflammatory and apoptosis processes. BX471 is a selective C-C chemokine receptor type 1 (CCR1) antagonist that showed a promising effect in modulating neuroinflammation in central nervous system (CNS) disorders. In this study, we investigated the neuroprotective effect of BX471 on the inflammatory pathway and apoptotic process in an in vitro model of induced-neuronal injury using SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells. Firstly, cytotoxicity was assessed by MTT assay to determine the optimal effective concentrations and the best temporal window for BX471 activity. Then, SH-SY5Y cells were subjected to a scratch injury to mimic a neuronal injury and were treated with different concentrations of BX471. ELISA and qRT-PCR were used to analyze the expression level of the CCR1/chemokines axis (CCR1, RANTES, MIP-1α), inflammatory markers (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, NF-κB, IκBα, and PPAR𝛾), and the apoptotic pathway (Bcl2, BAX, P53, and cleaved caspase 3). The results showed that BX471 significantly improved the cell viability and inhibited the CCR1/chemokine axis and pro-inflammatory cytokines as well as modulating the apoptotic course. Overall, these results suggest that BX471 may reduce neuronal injury by inhibiting neuroinflammation and apoptosis, and that its neuroprotective effect, mediated through the CCR1 signaling pathway, deserves further investigation in in vivo models.

title: Systems Toxicology Indicates AKT1/PTGS2-Centered Neuroinflammatory-Mitochondrial Crosstalk in Lidocaine Associated Neurotoxicity.
abstract: Lidocaine-containing teething gels are commonly used for pediatric oral analgesia, yet excessive exposure may induce severe neurotoxic effects, including seizure-related events. The molecular mechanisms underlying lidocaine-associated neurotoxicity remain poorly defined. We employed an integrative systems toxicology approach combining network toxicology, transcriptomic analysis (GSE143272), weighted gene co-expression network analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and experimental validation using Kamistad Gel extract at defined lidocaine-equivalent concentration to characterize the molecular basis of lidocaine-induced neurotoxicity. Sixteen shared targets were identified through the integration of lidocaine-related targets, epilepsy-associated genes, and transcriptomic signatures. AKT1 and PTGS2 emerged as key hub genes. Functional analyses consistently suggested neuroinflammatory signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction, and synaptic dysregulation as major pathogenic mechanisms. Molecular docking and 10-ns molecular dynamics simulations indicated stable interactions between lidocaine and AKT1/PTGS2. ROC analysis indicated moderate predictive performance of these genes in epilepsy datasets. In SH-SY5Y cells, Kamistad Gel extract significantly increased AKT1 and PTGS2 expression, supporting activation of inflammation-related neurotoxic pathways. Lidocaine-associated neurotoxicity may involve an AKT1/PTGS2-centered neuroinflammatory-mitochondrial crosstalk network accompanied by synaptic dysfunction. This study provides a systems-level mechanistic insight into lidocaine neurotoxicity and identifies potential targets for improving the safety of pediatric lidocaine-containing formulations.

title: Maternal Vitamin D Deficiency is Associated With Sex-Dependent Alterations in Neurodevelopment-Related Gene Expression, Particularly in the Hypothalamus.
abstract: Vitamin D (VD) is essential for calcium homeostasis and bone metabolism but also for brain development and function. However, few data are available on the impact of maternal VD deficiency (VDD) on sex-specific brain development, particularly in specific structures such as hypothalamus. This study investigated the impact of maternal VDD on early brain development, neuronal and glial differentiation, and hypothalamic gene expression in mice. Maternal VDD was associated with increased mRNA expression of markers related to neuronal differentiation and synaptogenesis in both sexes, while mRNA expression of astrocyte-related markers remained largely unchanged. Male offspring exhibited broader transcriptomic alterations, including dysregulation of melanocortin-pathway and synaptic signaling genes, in the hypothalamus of early postnatal and adult mice. Maternal VDD was associated with sex-dependent changes in gene expression relevant to early brain development, with altered mRNA expression of markers involved in neuronal differentiation and synaptogenesis in both sexes. Male offspring exhibited transcriptomic changes, including altered expression of melanocortin-pathway and synaptic signaling genes, further suggesting greater susceptibility of hypothalamic gene expression to maternal VDD. These findings indicate that maternal VDD may influence neurodevelopmental gene expression during early life, potentially contributing to later alterations in synaptic function, metabolism, and behavior.

title: Dynamic dopamine signaling, prediction error, and microcircuit mechanisms in stress-induced depression-like behaviors.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
abstract: Chronic stress contributes to major depressive disorder (MDD) phenotypes by disrupting coordinated neuromodulatory systems and their corresponding computational frameworks. In this review, we explore how the dynamic interplay of ventral tegmental area dopamine (DA) signaling, microcircuit gating, and prediction error mechanics orchestrates stress-induced depressive behaviors, such as anhedonia and amotivation. Rather than acting as the sole driver of depression, pathway-specific neuroadaptations across mesolimbic ( VTA → NAc ) and mesocortical ( VTA → PFC ) dopaminergic projections operate within a broader multi-transmitter landscape, interacting with serotonergic, noradrenergic, cholinergic, and glutamatergic/GABAergic systems. These signaling anomalies often translate into computational deficits in reinforcement learning, manifesting as blunted striatal reward prediction error (RPE) signals that scale directly with anhedonia severity. Chronic stress also disrupts cortical microcircuit gating governed by dopamine D 1 and D 2 receptors, inducing cellular senescence and collapsing ensemble synchrony within the prefrontal cortex and interconnected networks. Furthermore, specialized subcortical loops, including inputs from the nucleus accumbens (NAc), ventral hippocampus (vHIPP), lateral habenula (LHb), and locus coeruleus (LC), recalibrate overall susceptibility versus resilience by altering DA firing dynamics and population activity pools, often in a sex-specific manner. By bridging synaptic dopamine dynamics, subcortical prediction errors, and cortical ensemble synchrony, we propose a unified, multi-level framework demonstrating how stress-induced depressive behaviors result from a progressive breakdown in the brain's predictive coding and adaptive coping networks.

title: Automated Retinal Segmentation of Hyperspectral Images Using a Modified U-Net with Spectral Multi-head Attention.
journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) can capture spatial and spectral data of the retina. Retinal vessel segmentation enables quantitative analysis and assessment of retinal health. In this work, we developed an HSI system for mouse retina and a deep learning architecture to segment retinal vessels. Retinal images were manually segmented to establish ground truth. We proposed the use of multi-head attention block for the spectral data, as well as Tversky loss for segmentation refinement. The model's performance was assessed using Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and the Jaccard (IoU) metrics. A comparative analysis was conducted against the manual segmentation, and five other segmentation methods: UNet, UNet++, UNet3+, segment anything model (SAM), and SAM2. We demonstrated that our spectral network achieved an IoU and DSC scores of 0.80±0.04 and 0.89±0.02, respectively. Our network outperforms other networks. The automatic segmentation method provides a tool for retinal analysis and quantification.

title: Nanodelivery of Brucine in Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury: Mitochondrial PANoptosis, Cardiotoxicity, and Translational Barriers.
abstract: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury remains a major unresolved component of infarct expansion after timely restoration of coronary blood flow. Brucine, a toxic alkaloid from Strychnos nux-vomica L. is an instructive but experimentally constrained case study because low-exposure cardioprotective signals coexist with cardiac ion-channel liability and uncertain clinical dosing. This Review evaluates whether nanodelivery could widen the therapeutic window of brucine by reducing circulating free drug, enriching exposure near injured myocardium and enabling mechanistic testing of mitochondrial quality control, regulated cell death and antioxidant repair. The evidence base is mapped across direct brucine cardiovascular studies, direct brucine toxicology, brucine formulation studies outside cardiac reperfusion, non-brucine cardiac nanomedicine and general material-design principles. We emphasize that brucine-loaded nanomedicine has not yet been validated as a therapy for myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury; progress will require direct formulation-specific pharmacokinetics, myocardial biodistribution, hERG/QT safety, arrhythmia monitoring, large-animal efficacy and manufacturing-quality evidence.

title: The A-FABP Nexus in the Neurovascular Unit: Bridging Endothelial Barrier Breakdown and Microglial Lipotoxicity in Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: Ischemic stroke is a neurological cerebrovascular event characterized by highly complex, spatiotemporally dynamic pathophysiological processes. In recent years, stroke research has shifted from early isolated neuroprotection to the systematic investigation of the multidimensional homeostasis of the entire neurovascular unit (NVU). Within this complex pathological network, neuroinflammation mediated by cerebral lipid metabolic dysregulation has gradually emerged as an important contributor to NVU dysfunction and post-stroke secondary injury. Among various lipid chaperones, adipocyte fatty acid-binding protein (A-FABP) has attracted increasing attention because of its involvement in metabolic dysregulation, vascular injury, and neuroinflammation. This review comprehensively examines the emerging evidence for the multifaceted involvement of A-FABP in ischemic stroke. In the hyperacute phase, A-FABP acts as a potent endothelial disruptor, compromising the integrity of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) by activating MMP-9; Beyond this established vascular mechanism, findings from other experimental contexts suggest that A-FABP may also contribute to microglial lipid dysregulation and associated inflammatory responses, providing a potential mechanistic link between vascular injury and immune-metabolic dysfunction within the NVU. Preclinical studies further indicate that pharmacological inhibition or neutralization of A-FABP can attenuate ischemic brain injury; however, its therapeutic efficacy and safety in patients with ischemic stroke remain to be established. This review provides an in-depth analysis of the dynamic balance of the spatiotemporal effects of A-FABP, further highlighting its core value as a biomarker for poor stroke prognosis and a highly promising therapeutic target. It also examines current translational bottlenecks, including phase-specific intervention windows, applicability across different stroke subtypes, unresolved mechanisms of NVU crosstalk, and pharmacological optimization, aiming to provide directions for future investigation of A-FABP within the stroke immune-metabolic network.

title: Prophylactic Low-Dose Esketamine for Prevention of Intraoperative Penile Erection During Ureteroscopic Surgery Under General Anesthesia: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
abstract: Intraoperative penile erection (IPE) during ureteroscopic surgery may interrupt surgical procedures and increase the risk of urethral injury. Existing management strategies are largely reactive and frequently require rescue interventions after erection has already developed. Effective prophylactic strategies remain limited. We evaluated whether prophylactic esketamine reduces the incidence of intraoperative penile erection during ureteroscopic surgery under general anesthesia. This single-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial (Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500114505) enrolled 356 adult men (ASA I-II) scheduled for elective ureteroscopic surgery. Patients were randomized 1:1 to receive intravenous esketamine 0.3 mg/kg or saline before anesthetic induction; allocation was concealed, and patients, anesthetists, surgeons, and outcome assessors were blinded. The primary outcome was the incidence of IPE (Porst grade ≥1), assessed at nine predefined intraoperative time points (T0-T8), with rescue treatment for erections of grade ≥2. Secondary outcomes included erection severity, hemodynamic variables, recovery characteristics, and adverse events. The incidence of IPE was 6.2% (11/178) with esketamine versus 21.9% (39/178) with saline (RR 0.282, 95% CI 0.149-0.533; ARR 15.7%; NNT 6.4; P < 0.001). Porst grades were lower in the esketamine group during disinfection, ureteroscope insertion, and 10 min after surgery commenced, and fewer patients required rescue treatment for clinically significant erection (Porst grade ≥ 2, 4.5% vs 21.3%; P < 0.001). Mean arterial pressure was higher with esketamine intraoperatively (adjusted mean difference 3.49 mmHg), and heart rate was higher, without clinically significant hemodynamic disturbance. Recovery and adverse events did not differ significantly between groups, no hallucinations occurred; postoperative catheter-related bladder discomfort was less severe with esketamine (P < 0.001). Prophylactic low-dose esketamine was associated with a lower incidence and severity of intraoperative penile erection, without evidence of impaired postoperative recovery. These findings suggest that prophylactic esketamine may be a useful strategy for preventing this perioperative complication, warranting confirmation in larger multicenter trials.

title: Cariprazine Augmentation and Sustained Remission of Physical Aggression in Clozapine-Treated Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenia: A Case Report.
abstract: Persistent aggression may occur in treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) despite long-term clozapine treatment and multiple augmentation strategies. We describe a male patient in his sixties with a decades-long history of schizophrenia who required prolonged psychiatric inpatient care because of recurrent, unpredictable physical assaults toward other patients, staff, relatives, and police. This included treatment at a state forensic psychiatric hospital because of treatment complexity and safety concerns, not forensic legal status. Aggression persisted during adequately monitored high-dose clozapine treatment and several augmentation strategies. The last documented physical assault occurred in October 2021. Cariprazine 1.5 mg/day was initiated in November 2021, primarily for longstanding negative symptoms. Within approximately seven weeks, mood and participation in communal ward activities improved. No further physical assaults were documented during more than 4 years of follow-up. The patient subsequently transitioned to voluntary treatment and supported housing. Later somatic illnesses, temporary interruptions of oral medication, and substantial fluctuations in clozapine serum concentrations were not followed by renewed physical aggression. This case describes a prolonged temporal association between cariprazine augmentation and the absence of recurrent physical assaults, but the single-case design, episodic pretreatment course, concomitant treatment changes, and absence of standardized ratings preclude causal inference.

title: Effects of dance and music training on the plasticity of the core empathy network: intra- and inter-network connectivity.
abstract: Dance and music are two of the oldest and most universal forms of artistic expression, each requiring extensive training. Prolonged training is known to induce neuroplastic changes and enhance socio-emotional abilities such as empathy. The mirror neuron system (MNS) is associated with empathy; however, few studies systematically explored how dance and music training modulate the core empathy network, including subcortical regions within the limbic MNS. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data were obtained from 25 dancers, 24 musicians and 39 demographically matched control group (both groups are healthy). Core regions within relevant brain networks, along with key subcortical components of limbic MNS, specifically the amygdala and basal ganglia, were defined as regions of interest (ROIs) to build a core empathy network. Graph-theoretical metrics, including within-network degree (WND) and between-network degree (BND), were calculated to evaluate connectivity patterns. These metrics were further correlated with empathy scores. Both dancers and musicians exhibited altered connectivity within the core empathy network. Dancers showed increased WND and BND between basal ganglia regions and the ventral attention network, whereas musicians demonstrated enhanced WND between the amygdala and the subcortical network. Notably, both groups exhibited reduced WND between the superior frontal gyrus and the sensorimotor network. The neural changes were correlated with Interpersonal Reactivity Index (IRI) empathy subscale scores, indicating training-related modulations in affective and cognitive empathy. Dance and music training induce both distinct and overlapping patterns of neuroplasticity within the core empathy network that are associated with enhanced empathic ability. The findings support the potential of dance and music as systematic intervention programs.

title: Effects of Glucose and Vitamin D 3 on Heat Stress Resistance in a Caenorhabditis elegans Model of Polyglutamine Aggregation Disease.
abstract: Polyglutamine (polyQ) diseases are the most common form of inheritable neurodegeneration. Neuronal protein aggregates strongly correlate with polyQ symptoms; pathways that protect against protein aggregation may help mitigate the symptoms of poly-Q or delay disease onset. We used a C. elegans polyQ model, exposed to a heat stressor, to test potential protective mechanisms: glucose and vitamin D₃ (VD₃) supplementation. Glucose enrichment further shortened post-heat stress lifespan, while VD₃ in moderate doses trended toward restoring polyQ post-stress lifespan back to wild-type levels. These results show effects of early-life interventions that could indicate aspects of polyQ pathogenesis mechanisms and treatment options.

title: Assessing the construct validity of cross-national harmonized cognitive assessments using age.
abstract: Harmonized cognitive measures are key to cross-national comparisons of dementia risk. However, validating such measures cross-nationally is challenging due to differences in cognitive measures and a lack of a reference standard. Age, a characteristic strongly associated with cognition and widely measured, can serve as a benchmark for evaluating how well harmonized cognitive measures are broadly compatible with a common construct. We used cross-nationally harmonized measures from three studies in the US and five studies in England, Chile, Mexico, India, and South Africa (N = 27,317). Study-specific estimates of the association between general cognitive scores and age ranged from -0.040 to -0.075 SD units/year of age. The coefficient of variation was 24.1%, indicating moderate relative variability. Results support the hypothesis that cross-nationally harmonized scores, derived from partially overlapping test batteries, measure a broadly similar construct across countries. Future studies should further evaluate criterion, construct, and content validity of cognitive testing in cross-national populations.

title: A tool to evaluate the impact of lived experience involvement in research: the Brain and Genomics Hub Impact Log protocol.
abstract: Despite widespread recognition of the value of lived experience involvement (LEI) in healthcare research and increased LE involvement activity, we lack established implementation methods and instruments for reporting and evaluating impact. We present a protocol for an innovative LE-led Impact Log tool and LEI framework, which may help to address some fundamental barriers to LEI. The Impact Log will be implemented within a five-year multidisciplinary transdiagnostic research project on severe mental illness and is also designed for wider adaptation and use. We include a short literature review on LEI impact, to provide in-depth background. The Impact Log framework is designed to integrate inclusive impactful LEI throughout all research stages, and to use a short accessible form to record and evaluate impact across three domains: design and delivery; interpersonal and environmental aspects; systems and processes. Impact Log tool and LEI design and implementation is led by LE study leads and specialist LE advisory panel, with combined research experience and LE, fully integrated within the wider research team. All Hub research participants will be offered accessible opportunities for remunerated lived experience input, and there will be outreach to ensure diverse representation, aided by the Hub's charity partners. Data collection and analysis will be LE led and will include iterative analysis to inform continuing development. Diverse formal and informal dissemination throughout the project will maximise wider stakeholder engagement. The potential value of this research is to implement a novel tool and framework for facilitating, recording and evaluating LEI in complex mental health research, which can be adapted for wider use. Strengths in design are LE leadership and cross-cutting LE research integration, incorporation of multiple domains, and a focus on facilitating diversity and inclusion within LEI. Potential limitations for this project and wider adaptation may include limited resources, risk of bias and health challenges.

title: Pathological and Non-Pathological Severe Social Withdrawal Trait Profiles: Cluster Analysis and Predictors of Psychiatric Symptoms in Italian University Students.
journal: The International journal of social psychiatry
abstract: In recent years, the concept of hikikomori has been redefined due to profound socio-cultural and digital changes, making it necessary to distinguish between pathological and non-pathological forms of social withdrawal. This study aims to identify profiles of social withdrawal and describe their psychopathological correlates in a large sample of young Italian adults. A cross-sectional study was conducted on 2,303 Italian university students (aged 18-35), recruited through an online survey, using validated instruments for the assessment of social withdrawal (HQ-11), emotional distress (DASS-21), loneliness, boredom, alexithymia, and problematic use of the Internet and video games. Four distinct profiles were identified using k-means cluster analysis based on HQ-11 and DASS-21 subscales scores. Two clusters showed low levels of social withdrawal, with varying degrees of emotional symptoms, while two clusters showed high social withdrawal: one characterized by the absence of significant psychopathology ("non-pathological severe social withdrawal") and one associated with high emotional distress ("pathological severe social withdrawal"). The latter group reported significantly higher levels of loneliness, boredom, alexithymia, and problematic Internet use. Logistic regression analysis showed that difficulty in identifying emotions, high-arousal boredom, and high emotional loneliness were associated with classification into in the pathological severe social withdrawal trait profile. The results support the heterogeneity of self-reported severe social withdrawal traits and highlight the importance of distinguishing between profiles with higher and lower levels of associated psychological distress. However, these profiles should not be interpreted as clinically diagnosed hikikomori.

title: UK Dementia Trials Network: an expert-informed framework for improving representation in dementia trials.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia worldwide, yet clinical trials remain unrepresentative of those most affected. Ethnic minoritized groups, socioeconomically deprived communities, adults over 75, and populations in low- and middle-income countries are consistently underrepresented, limiting generalizability and reinforcing health inequities. This white paper draws on an international roundtable on Diversity and Inclusion in Dementia Trials, convened by the UK Dementia Trials Network at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference 2025. We determined that key barriers to research participation included geographic distance, financial burden, restrictive eligibility criteria, invasive procedures, and limited study partner support. We also highlight gaps in ethnic diversity and the inadequate integration of sex and gender considerations in trial design and reporting. Improving representation in AD trials is both a scientific and moral imperative. Achieving this requires coordinated action across community engagement and trust building, data transparency and reporting, global trial access and capacity building, eligibility criteria reform, and financial and logistical support for participants. We propose an expert-informed implementation framework derived from the roundtable that identifies actionable strategies, responsible stakeholders, measurable indicators, and expected implementation outcomes to support translation of our recommendations into practice.

title: Bipolar Disorder and Epilepsy: Clinical and Neurobiological Overlaps, Evidence Gaps, and an Exploratory Systems Perspective.
abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that bipolar disorder (BD) and epilepsy share important clinical, neurobiological, and therapeutic features. Both disorders are characterized by recurrent episodes and fluctuating clinical courses, raising the possibility that partially overlapping or analogous regulatory processes may contribute to some aspects of their clinical expression and progression. This review examines current evidence regarding the overlap between BD and epilepsy and explores integrative perspectives that may help explain their similarities. A narrative review of the literature was conducted. Evidence related to genetics, neuroimaging, cognition, neuroplasticity, neuroinflammation, stress biology, network neuroscience, and treatment response was examined. Findings across BD and epilepsy reveal partially overlapping biological and clinical features, including alterations in excitation-inhibition balance, neuromodulatory disturbances, neuroinflammatory processes, and neuroplastic changes. Neuroimaging studies in both conditions reveal abnormalities in large-scale brain networks involved in emotional regulation, cognitive control, and behavioral adaptation. Clinically, both disorders show sensitivity to environmental and physiological stressors and sleep disruption, cognitive impairment, and partial responsiveness to overlapping pharmacological and neuromodulatory interventions. These observations are compatible with the hypothesis that recurrent episodes and prolonged network dysregulation may reinforce maladaptive patterns of instability through interacting feedback processes, although this interpretation remains to be tested directly. Current evidence identifies several clinical and biological similarities between BD and epilepsy but does not yet establish that these similarities reflect identical or directly shared causal mechanisms. An integrative perspective combining network dysfunction, neuroplasticity, and systemic regulatory processes may provide a useful heuristic framework for investigating disease heterogeneity, progression, and treatment response. Further longitudinal and comparative studies are required before this perspective can support personalized monitoring strategies or mechanism-informed interventions.

title: Longitudinal associations between appearance-related social media consciousness and sleep in U.S. middle schoolers.
journal: Journal of research on adolescence : the official journal of the Society for Research on Adolescence
abstract: Social media use has been linked to poorer sleep outcomes in adolescents, yet the mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. Appearance-related social media consciousness (ASMC)-a preoccupation with one's appearance online-could relate to offline behaviors, including sleep. This study examined the association between ASMC and various sleep behaviors using a parallel mediation structural equation model. Participants were 1158 U.S. 8th-grade students (Mage = 13.14, 52% girls, 36% Hispanic/Latine, 37% qualified for free or reduced-price lunch) surveyed at two points across an academic year. Higher ASMC was indirectly associated with poorer sleep quality, increased sleep disturbances, and longer sleep onset latency through greater compulsive nighttime social media use. Additionally, higher ASMC was indirectly associated with earlier sleep onset times through longer morning routine durations. Findings suggest that appearance-related experiences on social media have implications for adolescent sleep health and provide preliminary support for some pathways through which its effects may occur.

Large-scale semantic indexing of Spanish biomedical literature using contrastive transfer learning.
abstract: The exponential growth of biomedical literature has made automatic indexing essential for advancing biomedical research. While automatic indexing has made strides in English biomedical literature, there has been limited research on non-English biomedical texts due to insufficient high-quality training data. We propose BERTDeCS, a novel deep learning framework for automatically indexing Spanish biomedical literature using contrastive transfer learning. BERTDeCS utilizes a multilingual BERT (M-BERT) to generate multi-language representations and adapts M-BERT for Spanish biomedical literature domain through contrastive learning. Additionally, BERTDeCS enhances its semantic indexing capabilities on Spanish biomedical literature by leveraging enriched English annotated literature in MEDLINE through transfer learning. Experimental results on Spanish datasets demonstrate that BERTDeCS outperforms state-of-the-art indexing methods, achieving top performance in the MESINESP and MESINESP2 Tasks on medical semantic indexing in Spanish within the BioASQ challenge. Additional experiments on Portuguese provide preliminary evidence that BERTDeCS can transfer to a closely related language sharing substantial lexical and biomedical terminology with Spanish. The source code is available at https://github.com/yourh/BERTDeCS and at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23212468.

title: A Gamified Mobile Application for Orthodontic Education: Usability Assessment and Impact on Knowledge and Attitude of Dental Students.
journal: European journal of dental education : official journal of the Association for Dental Education in Europe
abstract: The use of gamification-based educational interventions in dentistry has been proposed as a novel approach to increase cognitive engagement and improve learning; however, evidence regarding the simultaneous effect of these tools on students' knowledge and attitude in the field of orthodontics is limited. This study evaluated the usability of a gamified orthodontic application and compared its knowledge and attitude outcomes with traditional reference-book study. In an experimental study, 80 sixth-year dental students were assigned to the intervention and control groups. The intervention group used a gamified scenario-based application for 1 month. Usability was assessed with the Mobile Health App Usability Questionnaire (MAUQ). Knowledge and attitude scores were measured before and after the intervention, and data were analysed using a mixed linear model. The mean usability scores were assessed as satisfactory. Although both groups improved, significant time × group interactions favoured the intervention group for knowledge (p = 0.013) and attitude (p = 0.001). However, the observed effect sizes were small to moderate, suggesting a limited but potentially meaningful educational benefit. Orthodontic course grade showed a positive and significant association with both outcomes (p 0.05). Compared with traditional reference-book study, the gamified application was associated with modest improvements in knowledge and attitudes. However, the design did not allow the specific contribution of gamification to be distinguished from other digital-learning effects.

title: Which morphological skills predict development in vocabulary? Contrasting morphological awareness with morphological analysis.
abstract: Morphemes are the smallest units of meaning in language. This study examined which of two related morphological skills support vocabulary growth: morphological awareness (recognizing and manipulating morphemes) and morphological analysis (using morphemes to infer meanings). We studied 336 English-speaking children (F = 154, M = 182; Mage = 6 years and 8 months; 55% European, with <10% each Acadian, Asian, African, Aboriginal, and Middle Eastern). In Grade 1, children completed morphological awareness and analysis tasks, and controls of reading comprehension, word identification, phonological awareness, nonverbal ability, and working memory. Vocabulary was measured at Grades 1 and 4. Structural equation modeling revealed that only morphological analysis uniquely predicted gains in vocabulary.

title: Epigenetics in Traumatic Brain Injury.
abstract: Following traumatic brain injury (TBI), changes in proteins, metabolites, and gene expression are highly dynamic and are influenced by genetic and environmental factors, circadian rhythms, and injury characteristics, including injury type (focal or diffuse), severity (mild to severe), and stage of recovery (acute, subacute, and chronic). These molecular alterations are accompanied by epigenetic modifications that regulate gene expression and contribute to injury progression and recovery. In this review, we integrate and summarize preclinical and clinical studies examining DNA methylation, histone methylation and acetylation, microRNA (miRNA)-mediated regulation, RNA epigenetic modifications, and mitochondrial epigenetic (mitoepigenetic) changes following TBI. Most studies have focused on DNA methylation, histone modifications, and miRNAs in experimental models, providing important insights into cell type-specific epigenetic responses after injury. We also review studies evaluating therapeutic strategies, including DNA methyltransferase and histone deacetylase inhibitors, that target epigenetic mechanisms to improve TBI outcomes.

title: Nociplastic Questionnaire (NociQ): Development and Initial Validation.
abstract: Nociplastic pain is implicated in many chronic pain conditions, yet it has been defined primarily by the absence of structural causes-a diagnosis by exclusion. No validated nociplastic pain questionnaire exists. This study examined hypothesized pain-specific features of nociplastic pain and developed a brief self-report instrument, the Nociplastic Questionnaire (NociQ). We generated items based on literature review and input from experts and individuals with lived experience. We administered the items and measures of other pain-related constructs (pain intensity/interference, catastrophizing, kinesiophobia, and perceived stress) to 888 participants with diverse chronic pain conditions. Factor analyses supported four dimensions captured by internally consistent 4-item subscales (αs ≥0.74): 1) location variability, 2) exacerbation by thoughts and emotions, 3) widespreadness, and 4) allodynia. The NociQ total score adequately discriminated presumed nociplastic and non-nociplastic conditions (AUCs 0.73-0.75). Participants who had widespread pain or reported more presumed nociplastic conditions scored higher on all scales (ps <.001, ds=0.35-1.37). NociQ scales demonstrated small-to-moderate correlations with measures of theoretically distinct constructs (rs=0.10-0.44), supporting discriminant validity, and explained additional variance in pain intensity beyond those measures (ΔR²s=.02-.07; ps <.05), supporting incremental validity. Results indicate four nociplastic pain characteristics, including two, location variability and exacerbation by thoughts and emotions, psychometrically validated here for the first time. The 16-item NociQ demonstrates promising reliability and validity as a brief questionnaire of nociplastic pain. Future research should examine its clinical utility, such as in matching patients to pain mechanism-targeted treatments.
