'Leading by Leveraging Situations': A Participant Observation Study Exploring How Registered Nurses Lead Close to Older Adults in Municipal Home Healthcare.
journal: International journal of older people nursing
abstract: Leadership plays a crucial role in the quality of care and patient safety, especially in the context of strained resources. Municipal home healthcare is facing challenges, for example, fewer care workers to meet increasing care needs. Registered nurses are key figures in municipal home healthcare, and they are leaders in the direct care of older adults. There is a lack of knowledge of how registered nurses lead close to older adults. The aim of this study was to explore how registered nurses lead close to older adults in municipal home healthcare. Eight (n = 8) registered nurses participated in 50 h of participant observations. Meetings between registered nurses and older adults, and the time between these interactions, were observed to explore how the registered nurses lead close to older adults. Fieldnotes from observations and informal talks with the registered nurses were collected and analysed via reflexive thematic analysis. The leadership of registered nurses close to older adults was portrayed into three themes: (1) 'starting from the older adults' implies viewing the older adults holistically and prioritising their needs over the needs of the organisational system; (2) 'adapting to the particular', which entails tailoring the environment and themselves to the unique in each situation: and (3) 'utilising professional knowledge' to both prepare their leadership and to lead. These three themes support an overarching theme showing how registered nurses lead close to older adults by 'leveraging situations' encountered in their work. This study provides insights into registered nurses' leadership close to older adults in home healthcare. The participant observations revealed that this leadership entails leveraging situations within the organisational framework, implying a need for registered nurses' flexibility and the ability to adapt to the prerequisites in this sector to provide good and safe care. These findings indicate it is time for organisations to align care for older adults and those who provide and lead the care. The findings illustrate how registered nurses enact leadership close to older adults through situated and adaptive practices in direct nursing care. The adaptive leadership practices of registered nurses might impact the quality of care. Providing registered nurses with the prerequisites to lead close to older adults, through means such as guidelines and educational efforts, might contribute to the long-term sustainability of municipal home healthcare. Insights gained from this study indicate that RNs' leadership in HCC is performed by leveraging situations in their workday, which might be disguising potential consequences of a task-focused organization. This could affect the quality of care and RNs' work satisfaction. Subsequently, this study might affect the sustainability of HHC as a growing sector. Future research should explore how leadership contributes to sustainable development by balancing quality of care, health economic considerations and environmental impacts. RNs can apply the findings from this study to recognize and gain valuable insights in their own work. Decision-makers and educators should recognize how leadership is performed by RNs close to older adults. Facilitating educational efforts might advance RNs' leadership skills and competence, thereby enhancing the quality of care and contributing to the long-term sustainability of this growing sector in the future.

title: Genetic Screening for Expanded FMR1 Alleles in a Moroccan Cohort With Unexplained Intellectual Disability.
journal: Journal of intellectual disability research : JIDR
abstract: Intellectual disability (ID) constitutes a major neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD), arising from diverse genetic and environmental aetiologies. Fragile X syndrome (FXS), caused by CGG repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene, is one of the most common inherited causes of ID and autism. In Morocco, FMR1 molecular screening data are currently not available. This study provides the first characterisation of FMR1 mutations in Moroccan patients with nonsyndromic ID (NS-ID). One hundred children and adolescents (75 boys and 25 girls) were tested using AmplideX PCR/CE FMR1 Kit based on fluorescent triplet-primed PCR (TP-PCR) and capillary electrophoresis (CE) to determine CGG repeat sizes. A total of 92% of individuals (23 females and 69 males) carried an FMR1 allele within the normal CGG repeat range ( 200. As the first molecular screening initiative targeting FXS in high-risk patients, our results demonstrate the utility of testing in this population highlighting the importance of future multicentre studies.

title: Clinical features of mental imagery in substance use disorders: A mixed-methods analysis.
abstract: To characterise the frequency, features and content of craving-related mental imagery among people seeking treatment for substance use disorders (SUDs); examine within-session change in self-reported craving following imagery elicitation; and explore perceived links with autobiographical memory, behavioural, cognitive and emotional responses and imagery triggers. Mixed-methods observational study incorporating a semi-structured interview and repeated within-session measurement of craving, with quantitative analyses and qualitative content analysis. A single National Health Service adult community drug and alcohol treatment service in South London, United Kingdom. Fifty-five adults meeting Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition (DSM-5) criteria for SUD were recruited between June and December 2019; 33 (60.0%) met criteria for more than one SUD. The interview assessed craving-related imagery frequency, sensory and affective characteristics, content, autobiographical-memory links, perceived responses and triggers. Craving was measured using the Craving Experience Questionnaire ̶ Strength (CEQ-S11) at baseline, immediately after imagery elicitation and at the end of the interview. Fifty-one participants (92.7%) reported craving-related imagery. The predominant modality was visual in 49/51 (96.1%); among 50 participants with complete imagery data, 42 (84.0%) described recurrent imagery and 26 (52.0%) reported experiencing it daily. Forty-seven (94.0%) perceived their image as representing an actual event or as strongly associated with autobiographical memory, usually an amalgamation of multiple memories. The 51 images were classified into five overlapping themes: stages of substance consumption (80.4%), the substance itself (84.3%), imagery features (94.1%), sensory experiences and activation (84.3%) and contextual or setting features (96.1%). Among 211 reported triggers, places (21.8%), people (19.9%) and internal moods (17.5%) were most frequent. Mean CEQ-S11 scores were 39.50 at baseline, 48.70 immediately after imagery elicitation and 36.70 at interview end, with an overall effect of time, F(2, 100) = 5.03, P-value 0.008. Among participants with recurrent imagery, 31/42 (73.8%) reported often or always wanting to use the substance following the image, and 34/42 (81.0%) reported that the image often or always persisted until distraction or substance use. In a mixed-methods study of adults attending a community drug and alcohol treatment service, craving-related mental imagery was commonly reported and was predominantly visual, often recurrent, closely linked to autobiographical memory and associated with perceived urges to use substances.

title: Content Analysis of Free Online Information and Support Available to Young Dementia Carers Across Europe.
abstract: The aim of this study was to gain insight into young dementia carer-specific content provided on the websites of dementia and (young) carers organizations in seven European countries including: the UK, the Netherlands, Italy, Greece, Portugal, Ireland and Sweden. Research questions were: 1). What types of young dementia carer-specific content are available on national websites of dementia and (young) carers organizations across Europe? and 2). How does the content address the complex impact that dementia can have on young dementia carers? The identification of websites was informed by the contextual characteristics of each country in relation to dementia and young carers support and services. A standard protocol describing the website inclusion and exclusion criteria, data extraction and content analysis using a categorical coding framework was followed. Descriptive statistics were calculated to summarize data within and across countries. A total of 312 organizations with active websites meeting the eligibility criteria across countries were identified, and their websites reviewed. Content relevant to young dementia carers was identified in 28% (n = 86) of the websites, with uneven availability of resources across Europe and very limited resources in some countries. Most contents addressed five categories: Diagnosis & symptoms, Uncertainty & family distress, Changes in roles, Stigma & isolation and Identifying need for support. A lack of tailored resources to support young dementia carers was identified, particularly in relation to two categories: Grief & loss and Education & life planning. Only a minority of websites included young dementia carer-specific content. These websites primarily focused on general support needs and explanations of dementia, while key areas such as guidance on school, career, and life planning remain underdeveloped. There is a need for greater recognition of young dementia carers, clearer terminology, and more developmentally appropriate and practically oriented resources to strengthen online support for these carers across Europe.

title: Pharmacokinetics and Safety of Deuremidevir Hydrobromide (JT001) in Subjects with Mild and Moderate Renal Impairment: An Open-Label, Parallel-Group Phase I Study.
abstract: JT001 (deuremidevir hydrobromide, VV116) is an oral antiviral prodrug that is rapidly converted in vivo to its active metabolite, 116-N1. Since 116-N1 is mainly cleared by the kidneys, renal impairment may increase its systemic exposure. This study evaluated the pharmacokinetics of 116-N1 following a single 0.3-g oral dose of JT001 in participants with mild or moderate renal impairment and matched healthy controls. Absorption was generally similar across groups, with comparable time to peak concentration. However, declining renal function increased exposure to 116-N1 and slowed its elimination. Terminal half-life increased from 5.31 to 8.13 and 11.2 h in mild and moderate impairment. Apparent oral clearance decreased from 34.3 L/h in healthy participants to 21.4 and 13.8 L/h in patients with mild and moderate renal impairment, respectively. Twenty-four participants (eight per renal function group) were enrolled. Geometric mean AUC0-t increased by 63% in participants with mild renal impairment (geometric mean ratio [GMR] 163.31%, 90% CI 135.99%-196.12%) and by 157% in those with moderate renal impairment (GMR 257.42%, 90% CI 214.35%-309.13%), whereas Cmax remained comparable between groups. JT001 was generally well tolerated, with no serious or grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events. To further assess clinical relevance of these findings, the renal impairment data were incorporated into an updated population pharmacokinetic model. Simulations suggested that the approved regimen was suitable for patients with mild renal impairment, whereas a reduced regimen of 300 mg twice daily on Day 1 followed by 200 mg twice daily on Days 2-5 was recommended for patients with moderate renal impairment.

title: Beliefs about emotions, distress tolerance and paranoia across the menstrual cycle in individuals with premenstrual difficulties and controls.
journal: The British journal of clinical psychology
abstract: Premenstrual Disorders are characterized by recurrent symptoms associated with clinically significant distress or impairment. There is limited understanding of psychological processes associated with premenstrual difficulties. This study investigated maladaptive beliefs about emotions, distress tolerance and social-cognitive experiences of paranoia in individuals with premenstrual difficulties and controls across cycle phases. 109 participants provided data at four timepoints across two menstrual cycles. Participants were classified into PSST-defined provisional PMDD, moderate-to-severe PMS and control groups. Psychological outcomes were assessed during perimenstrual (cycle days 1-2) and mid-follicular (cycle days 4-8) phases across two cycles. Differences across assessment timepoints and groups were examined using linear mixed-effects models. In the provisional PMDD group, maladaptive beliefs about emotions were higher and distress tolerance lower at perimenstrual assessments than at mid-follicular assessments and controls perimenstrually. Ideas of reference were also higher at perimenstrual assessments than at mid-follicular assessments and controls perimenstrually. Ideas of persecution did not show the perimenstrual increase in either premenstrual difficulties group. Phase-related changes were not consistently observed in the moderate-to-severe PMS group or controls. Mid-follicular maladaptive beliefs about emotions and ideas of reference did not differ significantly between premenstrual difficulties groups and controls; however, distress tolerance remained lower in the provisional PMDD group than in controls. The provisional PMDD group showed higher perimenstrual maladaptive beliefs about emotions and ideas of reference, alongside lower distress tolerance. These findings suggest these processes may be relevant to more severe premenstrual difficulties. Prospective daily assessments are needed to clarify the temporal relationships between these processes and symptom severity.

title: Arhgef1 Deletion Disrupts Early Cortical Neurogenesis via PAK1 Overactivation and Causes Motor Dysfunction in Adulthood.
abstract: Precise regulation of early cortical development is essential for the establishment of normal brain function, and its disruption can contribute to the pathogenesis of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Impaired motor function is a prominent early manifestation of various NDDs, yet the mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified ARHGEF1, a Rho family guanine nucleotide exchange factor highly expressed during early corticogenesis, as a novel regulator in embryonic cortical neurogenesis and adult motor function. By Emx1-Cre-mediated forebrain deletion of Arhgef1 in mice (Arhgef1 cKO mice), early cortical neurogenesis is specifically disrupted, leading to reduced deep-layer cortical neurons. Mechanistically, Arhgef1 deficiency overactivates RAC1/CDC42-PAK1-Cofilin signaling in early cortical development, whereas pharmacological PAK1 inhibition within this critical window rescues the genesis of deep-layer cortical neurons. Importantly, Arhgef1 cKO mice exhibit remarkable motor learning and coordination deficits in adulthood, accompanied by altered neuronal morphology in the motor cortex and impaired neuronal activities in motor circuits. In all, we elucidate a critical developmental window when ARHGEF1 governs corticogenesis via negatively regulates PAK1-dependent pathway and further reveal an important role for ARHGEF1 in maintaining normal motor function in adulthood.

title: Synthesis of Nitrogen-Containing Heterocyclic Scaffolds and Applications in Scaffold Hopping: Development of an Aripiprazole Analog.
abstract: Heteroaromatic ring systems play a crucial role in drug development because they modulate physicochemical properties and expand the range of molecular interactions compared to non-heterocyclic aromatic rings. They are also widely represented among approved drugs. Among heteroatoms, nitrogen is the most prevalent in the diverse scaffold space of heterocyclic drugs, including those generated by fragment-based drug discovery approach. In this work, we show the synthesis of a set of novel or underexplored nitrogen heterocyclic fragments, obtained in three to five steps in moderate yields. In total, 12 fused [6,6] saturated/unsaturated bicycles were synthesized, which fulfill the general rule of fragment-like compounds. These heterocycles increased the fragment space of the CRAFT library and showed potential application in scaffold-hopping strategies for drug design. As a proof of concept, 2,6-naphthyridin-3-ol 2 was used to replace the 7-hydroxy-3,4-dihydroquinolin-2(1H)-one core of aripiprazole 41, generating 3-(4-(4-(2,3-dichlorophenyl)piperazin-1-yl)butoxy)-2,6-naphthyridine 40, that effectively blocked cocaine-induced hyperactivity in rodents at 20 mg/kg without inducing catalepsy, displaying a pharmacological profile similar to aripiprazole and demonstrating promising antipsychotic potential.

title: Vascular drivers of cerebrospinal fluid movement and enlarged perivascular spaces.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Perivascular spaces (PVSs) facilitate cerebrospinal fluid flow and waste clearance, which are critical for maintaining brain homeostasis. Enlarged PVSs (ePVSs) are an emerging marker of cerebral small vessel disease and are implicated in protein accumulation, neurodegeneration, and cognitive decline. While prior reviews have described the anatomy and correlates of ePVSs, the vascular mechanisms that drive perivascular fluid dynamics, and how their dysfunction might lead to ePVSs, have not been reviewed. This review examines how vascular mechanisms drive perivascular fluid dynamics and discusses how their impairment may contribute to ePVS formation and their impact on cognition. We propose an integrated vascular-ePVS hypothesis in which early vascular dysfunction may contribute to impaired waste clearance and ePVS burden, potentially linking early-life vascular health with later proteinopathy and cognitive decline. Elucidating the vascular contributions to ePVSs is imperative to identify therapeutic targets to preserve cognition in Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.

title: Parkinson Disease Subtype Stability and Eventual Convergence.
journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
abstract: Previous research identified distinct Parkinson disease (PD) clinical subtypes of "Motor Only," "Psychiatric & Motor," and "Cognitive & Motor" based on comprehensive, multidomain classification. Whether these subtypes reflect distinct trajectories or progressive disease stages remains unknown. This study aimed to determine the longitudinal stability of PD subtype membership. This study included 250 PD participants with baseline subtype classifications and behavioral evaluations at two timepoints (average interval = 2.51 years), including motor, cognitive, and psychiatric assessments. Latent transition analyses tested the stability of PD subtype membership over time, and logistic regression models examined baseline factors associated with subtype transitions. Available brain autopsy data from 67 participants strengthened analyses by allowing the exclusion of 9 participants with non-PD neuropathologic diagnoses (e.g., Multiple System Atrophy, Progressive Supranuclear Palsy). The three baseline subtypes ("Motor Only," "Psychiatric & Motor," and "Cognitive & Motor") persisted at the second timepoint. Individuals in the "Motor Only" subtype at baseline had a high probability of remaining in the same subtype at follow-up (0.91), demonstrating longitudinal stability. Participants in the "Psychiatric & Motor" and "Cognitive & Motor" subtypes remained in the same subtype with probabilities of 0.55 and 0.59, respectively. A fourth "Severe Multidomain" subtype emerged at follow-up, characterized by more pronounced motor, cognitive, and psychiatric dysfunction. 64% of the "Severe Multidomain" group had dementia, compared with ≤ 7% in the other three subtypes. Subsequent analyses indicated that higher baseline Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) sum of boxes was strongly associated with transition to a different subtype. These findings suggest that PD subtypes reflect relatively stable subgroups that may eventually converge with development of dementia.

title: Need for a definitive trial of local versus general anaesthesia in chronic subdural haematoma; survey and literature review of ongoing trials.
abstract: Chronic subdural haematoma (cSDH) is a common neurosurgical condition, many patients have significant comorbidity or are living with frailty. Surgery is effective and can be performed under local anaesthesia (with or without sedation) (LAS) or general anaesthesia (GA). Optimal technique for both GA and LAS is poorly defined but similar questions have been explored in other surgical settings. We sought to clarify the breadth of evidence for anaesthetic technique in cSDH surgery, while drawing on relevant literature from other disciplines to understand how a definitive trial of this question could be performed. We used a combination of review of trial registries, the Cochrane database, and a survey of anaesthetic and neurosurgical practitioners. We identified a paucity of high-quality studies, especially randomised trials, exploring this question. The literature, and survey of anaesthetists and surgeons suggest that LAS may achieve equivalent outcomes, but significant confounding exists in current studies. Registered trials are single centre, and Cochrane reviews in other fields present issues of equipoise, study design, and outcome choice as key challenges in designing a definitive trial. There is significant interest in this topic as evidenced by published and emerging literature and views of anaesthetists and surgeons. No registered trial is multi-centre or draws on challenges identified in similar trials from other disciplines.

title: Genome-wide analysis identifies pleiotropic genes shared between severe mental disorders and biomarkers of cellular aging.
abstract: Severe mental disorders such as bipolar disorder (BD), major depressive disorder (MDD) and schizophrenia (SZ) are characterized by reduced life expectancy, premature mortality and alterations of aging biomarkers, leading to hypothesize that they might be associated with accelerated cellular aging. We quantified the genetic overlap between severe mental disorders and a comprehensive set of aging biomarkers including multivariate longevity and healthy aging (mvAge), brain age gap (BAG), leucocyte telomere length (gLTL), mitochondrial DNA copy number and epigenetic age acceleration (gEAA) using cutting-edge methods, and evaluated their functional enrichment and suitability as drug targets. All disorders were negatively correlated with mvAge. Further, MDD correlated negatively with gLTL and positively with gEAA. We identified several pleiotropic variants, with nine genes (AC068490.2, ASIC2, CNNM2, FURIN, GPM6A, HS6ST3, RP5-1043L13.1, SORCS3 and SP4) containing variants shared between aging biomarkers and all disorders. Functional analyses with summary-data-based Mendelian randomization showed that increased expression of the druggable gene CRHR1 in the prefrontal cortex was associated with increased risk of MDD and BAG measures. Our findings suggest that shared heritability might contribute to reduced longevity and healthy aging in severe mental disorders and identify pleiotropic genes involved in synaptic function and metabolic processes related to micronutrients such as folate and magnesium.

title: Bridging the gap: advanced chromatin biotechnologies for circadian epigenomic profiling in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy remain the main therapies for treating head and neck cancers, however new modalities have emerged with an emphasis to understand the complexity of the tumor biology. One emerging layer of complexity is the circadian clock, disrupted in many cancers, contributes to pathogenesis and progression due to its crosstalk with cancer pathways. While transcriptional alterations of core clock genes have been described in Head and Neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), the higher-order epigenetic and chromatin-based mechanisms underlying circadian dysregulation remain poorly defined. In this review, we highlight the potential of several chromatin-based biotechnologies in characterizing circadian clock disruption and identifying epigenetic biomarkers in HNSCC. Powerful assays including Chromatin conformation capture, Chromatin immunoprecipitation, DNA methylation profiling, ATAC-seq and single cell technologies can dissect circadian disruption at multiple regulatory layers. These approaches enable genome-wide mapping of chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and 3D chromatin organization. Integrating these approaches across HPV-positive (HPV+) and HPV-negative (HPV-) HNSCC provides a framework to determine whether circadian disruption reflects transcriptional deregulation alone or involved structural genome remodeling that actively drives tumor progression. Linking circadian disruption to epigenomic reprogramming in HNSCCs can serve to identify mechanisms of therapeutic resistance and identify vulnerabilities. Advancing chromatin-informed circadian biomarker discovery in HNSCC has the potential to shift precision oncology from static genomic profiling toward dynamic, architecture-based epigenetic regulation.
